headline: Apple iPhone Duo reviews are in: A first-class foldable with a matte inner display
summary: Reviewers praise the first-class foldable design and its unique matte inner display, marking a significant evolution for Apple's smartphone line.
details: The iPhone Duo represents the most significant shift in iPhone's form factor in nearly two decades, introducing Apple's first foldable design. Reviewers highlight its innovative approach to smartphone design.
Many outlets praise the device as a 'first-class foldable,' with particular appreciation for its unique matte inner display. This finish reportedly enhances the user experience by reducing glare.

Despite innovative features, some reviews describe the iPhone Duo as a 'messy, expensive, good time,' suggesting a premium price point and a learning curve. It aims to combine cutting-edge technology with Apple's signature user experience.
caption:
Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, is here, and reviews are calling it the biggest change to the iPhone in 20 years.

The iPhone Duo represents the most significant shift in iPhone's form factor in nearly two decades, introducing Apple's first foldable design. Reviewers highlight its innovative approach to smartphone design.

Many outlets praise the device as a 'first-class foldable,' with particular appreciation for its unique matte inner display. This finish reportedly enhances the user experience by reducing glare.

Despite innovative features, some reviews describe the iPhone Duo as a 'messy, expensive, good time,' suggesting a premium price point and a learning curve. It aims to combine cutting-edge technology with Apple's signature user experience.

headline: AMD and Intel unify PyTorch CPU optimization via oneDNN
summary: The UXL Foundation's oneDNN library will now support both AMD and Intel CPUs for PyTorch AI inference, simplifying development.
details: Intel and AMD are collaborating to integrate their CPU optimizations for PyTorch into a single library, oneDNN. This unified approach will offer tuning for both AMD and Intel chips, streamlining the AI inference process for developers.

AMD's ZenDNN, a downstream version of oneDNN, is being merged into the open-source oneDNN library, which is managed by the UXL Foundation and driven by Intel. AMD has also joined the UXL Foundation as a steering member, contributing $20,000 annually.

This unification effort was recommended by the x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group (EAG), a joint initiative between Intel and AMD. The oneDNN backend is crucial for accelerating CPU inference workloads in frameworks like PyTorch, having previously shown significant performance improvements.

The oneDNN library dynamically detects hardware features at runtime to generate optimized kernels for specific platforms and supports low-precision data types essential for AI and machine learning operations. This ensures developers can achieve optimal performance regardless of the underlying hardware.

For developers, this collaboration means a single backend can provide the necessary optimizations for PyTorch across diverse systems. While the current focus is on x86 architectures, oneDNN is a cross-platform library that also supports Arm and RISC-V architectures.
